Cautiously supportive, with added financial-stability caution per the FSR. The strong labor market and “moderate” activity justify holding at 1.50–1.75%, while below-target inflation and low market-based inflation compensation keep the stance dovish-neutral. The FSR highlights elevated nonfinancial corporate leverage (including leveraged loans and BBB concentrations) and underwriting risks, which amplify downside risks and echo the statement’s weakness in business investment and exports. The September 2019 repo market stress noted in the FSR underscores funding-market vulnerabilities; accordingly, the announced Treasury bill purchases and repo operations are best seen as ample-reserves implementation to ensure money market functioning, not new QE. The FSR also points to generally solid bank capital and manageable household vulnerabilities, which temper tail risks but do not offset valuation and credit concerns. Balancing these, the tone remains growth-supportive but more guarded once FSR vulnerabilities are incorporated.
